articles.title: Hilariously Fast Volume Computation with the Divergence Theorem
articles.summary: The Divergence Theorem allows for the computation of volume in a simple 3D mesh by summing the surface integrals of a vector field over the mesh's surface. This is achieved by first defining the vector field and its divergence, and then using the theorem to equate the volume integral to the surface integral of the vector field. This approach is particularly useful for triangulated meshes, where the vector field can be represented as the gradient of a scalar function.
